title: At 16, Adi Altschuler founded an inclusive youth movement, and the UN chose it as a special advisor

trailer.text: Adi Altschuler is the founder of the Krembo Wings youth movement, and in 2014 TIME magazine named her one of six future world leaders.
Krembo Wings is an Israeli youth movement for children and teens with and without disabilities.
The movement was founded in 2002 by Adi Altschuler, a 16-year-old girl.
Teenage boys and girls lead the activities, and the movement is open to all communities in Israel.
In July 2018, the UN's ECOSOC council granted the movement special consultative status.
According to Wikipedia, it has about 100 branches in Israel today.

glance.label: Recognition
glance.value: Special consultative status at the UN's ECOSOC, 2018

stations.title: One child and a bag of Krembos

paragraphs.text: Even before there was a movement, Adi Altschuler volunteered with a young child with cerebral palsy, Kfir Kobi.
According to Wikipedia, the volunteering was at the ILAN organization.
When she was 16, Altschuler founded the movement.
The first branch began as a small group of children with and without disabilities in Hod Hasharon.
According to the Jerusalem Post, when the movement began in 2002, the first counselors brought a bag of Krembos.
Children with special needs can easily eat Krembos.
Talia Harel Bejerano, the movement's CEO, said in a CTech article from October 2024 that she had arrived at the movement 16 years earlier as its first employee.
Teenage boys and girls lead the movement's activities.
According to ISRAEL21c, counselors can be as young as 12, and about 25 percent of the counselors have a disability themselves.
An experienced counselor aged 16 to 18 runs each branch.
The counselors wear the same uniform as the children they lead, and pay the same membership fee.
According to Wikipedia, the only adults in the branch are an adult coordinator, usually a university student in their 20s, and a nursing worker.
The participants travel to and from the activities in accessible transport with escorts.
Every branch has a nursing caregiver who helps the participants.
According to Wikipedia, the movement holds an accessible summer camp every summer.

stations.title: Who comes, and what difference it makes

paragraphs.text: According to JTA, the movement developed a model that integrates children with severe disabilities with teens without disabilities.
According to ISRAEL21c, it is the only inclusive youth movement in Israel.
The movement accepts children and teens with all types of disabilities.
According to the Jerusalem Post, the movement is open to all communities in Israel, unlike regular youth movements.
It includes secular and religious Jews, Muslims, Christians, Bedouins, Druze and new immigrants.
According to JTA, the movement has branches in Druze, Muslim, Christian and Bedouin communities.
The movement's CEO said that children with special needs are not found in playgrounds, but sit at home, and the activities take them outside.
Merav Boaz said that the movement has teens who had never celebrated a birthday with people outside their family.
According to the CEO, parents said the children began taking responsibility at home, tidying their room and putting effort into their studies.
In 2004 the movement received the Ramon Award, then called the Tamari Award, for quality, leadership and excellence.
In 2008, on the 60th Independence Day, a representative of the movement lit a beacon.
In 2009 Altschuler and the movement received the Presidential Award for Volunteerism.
In 2014 TIME magazine named Altschuler one of six future world leaders.

stations.title: From Hod Hasharon to the UN

paragraphs.text: According to ISRAEL21c, the movement's leaders were invited to the UN to talk about the Israeli initiative.
Merav Boaz said the movement has hosted delegations from social and educational organizations from many countries.
According to Calcalist, the movement's evaluation studies paved its way to the UN.
The studies show how much the movement influences the perceptions of the mentors.
On 24 July 2018, the UN's ECOSOC council decided to grant special consultative status to 210 non-governmental organizations.
The movement appears on the list under the name Krembo Wings, RA.
Calcalist wrote that this is an unprecedented achievement for the movement, in the field of integration and inclusion.
According to the ECOSOC website, this status is granted to organizations with special expertise.
Such organizations can participate in many events, including the sessions of ECOSOC and its commissions.
The movement's CEO said the status makes it possible to attend conferences and to spread the movement's knowledge.
According to the Jerusalem Post, the movement will be able to present its model and advise other countries.

stations.title: Growing, and there is still a waiting list

paragraphs.text: According to Wikipedia, the movement has about 100 branches in Israel.
According to a sponsored article in CTech, since 7 October the movement has been running activities for children with disabilities in more than 500 hotels and facilities.
The CEO said the movement set up three daily activity centers in evacuee areas.
In 2018 the CEO said there was a waiting list of 3,000 children whom they had not managed to admit to the activities.
The chairman of the board said he is concerned about the children waiting for new branches.
He added that the movement will do everything to speed up the process, despite the economic challenges.
According to the CEO, 50 local authorities want a branch, but the movement has no money for it.
A branch costs 300 thousand shekels a year, and no branch is opened without at least 100 thousand shekels from the local authority.
She said there is potential for 250 branches in the country.
According to ISRAEL21c, the movement's annual budget at the time was $6.2 million, and its sources were donations, membership fees, government ministries and local authorities.
In 2018 the CEO told Calcalist that the budget is 30 million shekels a year, and that the Welfare Ministry supported the growth.
According to CEO Talia Harel Bejerano in a CTech article, most of the movement's annual budget comes from public and private donations.
According to Walla, in 2018 the movement faced complete closure, because of a budget dispute between the Labor Ministry and the Finance Ministry.
The CEO said the movement is working with the state to receive official recognition as a youth movement.
According to the movement, in an article published in CTech, donations to the movement decreased significantly following the war.
According to the movement's announcement, government support fell by about 50% compared with previous years.
According to Walla, the movement announced on social media that it would not hold its annual summer camp that year. According to the movement, the reason is a cut in government support.
According to Walla, the Ramat Hasharon municipality approved a budget to fund the summer camp for the city's children.

The Ministry of Welfare stated that in 2021 it increased support for inclusive leisure nonprofits from 11.5 to 18.5 million shekels. According to the ministry, in 2022 the budget was returned to its original size and divided among more nonprofits, and this decision also affected the movement's budget.
MK Tali Gottlieb attacked the movement after the report on the cut.
She wrote on Twitter that in 2021 the movement had income of more than 44 million, and expenses of about 40 million.
According to Walla, three years earlier Yigal Canaan stirred a storm with a post attacking the movement.
The Givatayim branch coordinator, Gali Balali, was killed in the Nahal Tzafit disaster.

claims.text: מנכ"לית התנועה אמרה לכלכליסט שהתקציב הוא 30 מיליון שקל בשנה ושמשרד הרווחה תמך בצמיחה.
claims.quote: התקציב שלנו הוא 30 מיליון שקל בשנה. משרד הרווחה תמך בנו ואפשר לנו לצמוח מסיבית בשנים האחרונות

claims.text: לדברי המנכ"לית, רוב התקציב השנתי של התנועה מגיע מתרומות.
claims.quote: A majority of our annual budget comes from donations, both public and private.

claims.text: לפי וואלה, ב-2018 התנועה עמדה בפני סגירה מוחלטת בעקבות מחלוקת תקציבית בין משרד העבודה לאוצר.
claims.quote: בשנת 2018, התנועה עמדה בפני סגירה מוחלטת, לאחר שהתפתחה מחלוקת תקציבית בין משרד העבודה לאוצר

claims.text: לדברי המנכ"לית, התנועה פועלת מול המדינה לקבל הכרה רשמית כתנועת נוער.
claims.quote: אנחנו עובדים על זה מול המדינה ומקווים לקבל בהקדם הכרה רשמית כתנועת נוער.

claims.text: לפי CTech, בעקבות המלחמה התרומות לתנועה ירדו משמעותית.
claims.quote: Following the war, donations have decreased significantly, making it difficult to open the upcoming activity year.

claims.text: לפי הודעת התנועה, התמיכה הממשלתית ירדה בכ-50% משנים קודמות.
claims.quote: תקצוב התמיכה ממשרדי הממשלה השונים, ירד משמעותית, ועבור כנפיים של קרמבו מדובר בצניחה חדה של כ-50% משנים קודמות

claims.text: לפי הודעת התנועה בוואלה, מחנה הקיץ השנתי בוטל.
claims.quote: אנו נאלצות להודיע שלא נקיים השנה את מחנה הקיץ התנועתי, הנחשב למפעל השיא של כנפיים של קרמבו כבר למעלה מעשור

claims.text: לפי וואלה, עיריית רמת השרון אישרה תקציב למימון מחנה הקיץ לילדי העיר.
claims.quote: גם עיריית רמת השרון אישרה בעקבות ההודעה תקציב למימון מחנה הקיץ לילדי רמת השרון.

claims.text: משרד הרווחה מסר שבשנת 2021 הגדיל את תקציב התמיכות לעמותות פנאי משלב מ-11.5 ל-18.5 מיליון שקל.
claims.quote: בשנת 21 הגדיל המשרד את תקציב התמיכות לעמותות פנאי משלב לילדים עם מוגבלות מ-11.5 ל-18.5 מיליון שקל

claims.text: ח"כ טלי גוטליב תקפה את התנועה בעקבות הפרסום על הקיצוץ.
claims.quote: חברת הכנסת טלי גוטליב (הליכוד) תקפה את התנועה בעקבות הפרסום על הקיצוץ בתמיכה הממשלתית

claims.text: גוטליב כתבה בטוויטר שב-2021 הכנסות התנועה היו למעלה מ-44 מיליון והוצאותיה כ-40 מיליון.
claims.quote: בשנת 2021 ההכנסות לכנפיים של קרמבו היו למעלה מ-44 מיליון. הוצאות כ-40 מיליון. העמותה בעודף של ארבעה מיליון.

claims.text: לפי וואלה, יגאל כנען עורר לפני שלוש שנים סערה בפוסט שתקף את התנועה.
claims.quote: לפני שלוש שנים עורר כנען סערה כשהעלה פוסט לפייסבוק בו תקף את התנועה

claims.text: כלכליסט שאל על האירוע הטרגי שבו רכזת סניף גבעתיים גלי בללי נספתה באסון נחל צפית.
claims.quote: לפני כמה שבועות עברתם אירוע טרגי כאשר רכזת סניף גבעתיים גלי בללי נספתה באסון נחל צפית.

claims.text: לפי כל זכות, הפעילות מיועדת לחניכים מגיל 10.
claims.quote: הפעילות מיועדת לחניכים מגיל 10 עד סיום כיתה

claims.text: לפי כלכליסט, התנועה פועלת ב-66 סניפים ברחבי הארץ.
claims.quote: כנפיים של קרמבו הוקמה לפני 16 שנים ומקיימת כיום פעילות ארצית ב־66 סניפים

claims.text: לפי וואלה, לתנועה 92 סניפים ברחבי הארץ.
claims.quote: לתנועה 92 סניפים הפזורים ברחבי הארץ בכל המגזרים ומכל היכולות

claims.text: לפי כתבה ממומנת ב-CTech (2024), התנועה התרחבה ליותר מ-94 סניפים.
claims.quote: Since its inception two decades ago, the movement has expanded to over 94 branches across the country

quote_translations.c48: In each of the movement's branches there is a nursing caregiver who assists the participants.

quote_translations.c39: 50 local authorities want us to open a branch with them but we have no money for it.

quote_translations.c37: The potential is 250 branches in the country. To provide for every special and non-special child, the budget needs to grow threefold
quote_translations.c36: Our budget is 30 million shekels a year. The Welfare Ministry supported us and enabled us to grow massively in recent years

quote_translations.c41: We are working on this with the state and hope to receive official recognition as a youth movement soon.

quote_translations.c69: Following the announcement, the Ramat Hasharon municipality also approved a budget to fund the summer camp for the children of Ramat Hasharon.

quote_translations.c66: Member of Knesset Tali Gottlieb (Likud) attacked the movement following the report on the cut in government support
quote_translations.c67: In 2021 Krembo Wings' income was more than 44 million. Expenses about 40 million. The nonprofit is in a surplus of four million.

quote_translations.c54: A few weeks ago you went through a tragic event when the Givatayim branch coordinator Gali Balali was killed in the Nahal Tzafit disaster.

quote_translations.c19: Krembo Wings was founded 16 years ago and today runs nationwide activity in 66 branches
quote_translations.c56: The movement has 92 branches spread across the country in all sectors and of all abilities
